## loading in packages

```{r}
#loading in packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(rstatix)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

#extras for nice looking tables: 
install.packages("gt")
library(gt)
install.packages("gtExtras")
library(gtExtras)

```

## reading data

```{r}
#reading excel files: 
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")  #tells it to read NA as missing data 
```

## cleaning up data

### seedling height cleaning

```{r, HEIGHT CLEANING}

#dropping uneeded rows: 
TALL1 <- Height_Data_Raw |>  select(Date, Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, Dead_Alive, Notes)

#rename columns: 
TALL2 <- TALL1 |> rename( tdate = Date, 
                          tblock = Block, 
                          ttreatment = Treatment, 
                          ttag = Tag_Num, 
                          tsap_AB = Sapling_AB_etc, 
                          tht = Seedling_Ht_cm, 
                          dead_alive = Dead_Alive, 
                          notes = Notes
)

#reclassifying data types: 

#block, treatment, dead/alive: character --> factor
TALL3 <- TALL2 |> mutate(across
                         (c(tblock, ttreatment, dead_alive),
                           as.factor))

#date: charcter --> factor with levels 
TALL3 <- TALL3 |> mutate(tdate = as.factor(tdate), 
                         levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 

glimpse(TALL3) #double checking work 

#replacing OA in height: 
TALL3$ttreatment[TALL3$ttreatment=="OA"]<- "OS" #why the hell is it OA in this file only. who did this 

TALL4 <- TALL3 |> filter(ttreatment != "SA")  #removing rows with SA treatment, because what is that
TALL4 <- TALL4 |> drop_na(dead_alive) #removing the one NA row since it messes up my other graphs 
```

```{r}
#looking for height outliers 

boxplot(TALL4$tht, plot=FALSE)$out  #identifying height outlier values 

outliers <- boxplot(TALL4$tht, plot=FALSE)$out  #assigning these values to a vector

TALL5<- TALL4[-which(TALL4$tht %in% outliers),] #removing the outliers, reassigning data frame to TALL 5

TALL6 <- TALL5 |> group_by(ttreatment, tblock) |> mutate(block_treat_mean = mean(tht))

```

### soil moisture cleaning

```{r, SOILMOIST CLEANING}

#removing unecessary columns: 
MOIST1 <- Moist_Data_Raw |>  select(Date, Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc)

#rename columns: 
MOIST2 <- MOIST1 |> rename( mdate = Date, 
                            mblock = Block, 
                            mtreatment = Treatment, 
)

#reassign data type: 

#date: charcter --> factor with levels 
MOIST3 <- MOIST2 |> mutate(mdate = as.factor(mdate), 
                           levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 

#block and treatment: character --> factor
MOIST3 <- MOIST3 |> mutate(across
                           (c(mblock, mtreatment),
                             as.factor))


#VWC's: character --> numeric 
MOIST3 <- MOIST3 |> mutate(across
                           (c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), #select columns
                             as.numeric)) #converting 2 numerical 

glimpse(MOIST3) #checking work 

#add column with VWC average per row: 
MOIST4 <- MOIST3 |> rowwise() |> 
  mutate(vwc_mean = mean(
    c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE
  )) |> ungroup() 

#dropping extra NA rows 
MOIST5 <- MOIST4 |> drop_na(VWC1_perc)

```

```{r, removing unecessary objects}

rm(Height_Data_Raw, Moist_Data_Raw, MOIST1, MOIST2, MOIST3, SPAD_Data_Raw, TALL1, TALL2)
```

## Descriptive Stats for Height and Soil Moisture:

```{r}


#height summary: 

height_summ <- TALL6 |> group_by(ttreatment) |> 
  summarize(mean_height       = mean(tht, na.rm = TRUE), 
            sd_height         = sd(tht, na.rm = TRUE), 
            sample_sz_height  = n(), 
            se_height         = sd_height / sqrt(sample_sz_height)) |> 
  mutate_at(vars(mean_height, sd_height, se_height), # bonus line to reduce digits
            .funs = round, 2)
  

#soil moisture summary: 

moist_summ <- MOIST5 |> group_by(mtreatment) |> 
  summarize(mean_moist       = mean(vwc_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 
            sd_moist         = sd(vwc_mean, na.rm = TRUE), 
            sample_sz_moist  = n(), 
            se_moist         = sd_moist / sqrt(sample_sz_moist)) |> 
  mutate_at(vars(mean_moist, sd_moist, se_moist), # bonus line to reduce digits
            .funs = round, 2)


#summary tables all nice and pretty 

height_summ |> knitr::kable(caption = "Seedling Height Summary Table",  
                            col.names = (c("Treatment", "Mean", "Standard Deviation", "Sample Size", "Standard Error"))) 


moist_summ |> knitr::kable(caption = "Soil Moisture Summary Table", 
                           col.names = (c("Treatment", "Mean", "Standard Deviation", "Sample Size", "Standard Error"))) 


###setting up very nice and pretty tables: 

#height summary: 
height_gt <- gt(height_summ) |> tab_header(
  title = "Oak Seedling Height (cm) Summary Statistics by Microhabitat") |>  #setting title
  cols_label( ttreatment = "Microhabitat Type",  #changing column titles 
              mean_height = "Mean", 
              sd_height = "Standard Deviation", 
              sample_sz_height = "Sample Size", 
              se_height = "Standard Error" ) |>  
  tab_style( style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
locations = cells_column_labels(everything())) |>  #bolding column titles 

#replacing the treatment acronyms in height: 
sub_values(columns = ttreatment,
           values = "AC", replacement = "Adult Canopy") |> 
sub_values(columns = ttreatment,
           values = "DT", replacement = "Woody Debris") |> 
sub_values(columns = ttreatment,
           values = "NR", replacement = "Natural Recruit") |> 
sub_values(columns = ttreatment,
           values = "OS", replacement = "Open Space")

#soil moisture summary: 
moist_gt <- gt(moist_summ) |> tab_header(
  title = "Soil VWC % by Microhabitat") |>  #title time 
  cols_label( mtreatment = "Microhabitat Type",  #changing column titles 
              mean_moist = "Mean", 
              sd_moist = "Standard Deviation", 
              sample_sz_moist = "Sample Size", 
              se_moist = "Standard Error" ) |>  
  tab_style( style = list(cell_text(weight = "bold")),
             locations = cells_column_labels(everything())) |>  #bolding column titles
  #replacing the treatment acronyms in height: 
  sub_values(columns = mtreatment,
             values = "AC", replacement = "Adult Canopy") |> 
  sub_values(columns = mtreatment,
             values = "DT", replacement = "Woody Debris") |> 
  sub_values(columns = mtreatment,
             values = "NR", replacement = "Natural Recruit") |> 
  sub_values(columns = mtreatment,
             values = "OS", replacement = "Open Space")

#saving em: 
gtsave(height_gt, filename = "height_summ_table.png")

gtsave(moist_gt, filename = "moist_summ_table.png")
```

## ANOVA Analysis

### height data tim

```{r}

cols <- c("Dead" = "#DC3220", "Alive" = "#005AB5") #setting up specific colors for dead and alive 

survivor_bar <- TALL6 |> group_by(ttreatment) |> count(dead_alive) |>  ggplot() + 
  aes(x = ttreatment, y = n, fill = dead_alive) + 
  geom_col(position = "fill") + scale_fill_manual(
    values = cols, aesthetics = "fill"  #manually assigning the values to the colors from earlier 
  )  

survivor_bar + labs(  #assignign labels and titles for everything 
    title = "Seedling Survivorship by Microhabitat", 
    x = "Microhabitat Type", 
    y = "Survivorship", 
    fill = "Survival Status"
  ) + 
  scale_x_discrete( #renaming microhabitat types 
    labels = c("Adult Canopy", "Woody Debris", "Natural Recruit", "Open Space")
  )



ggsave(filename = "survivor_bar_plot.png",  plot = get_last_plot(), width = 6, height = 4)  #savin it 

#NR has highest number of alive seedlings, followed by AC, then DT
#OS has highest number of dead, followed by DT 
#NR with lowest amount of dead 
```

```{r, pre-ANOVA work}

##setting up ANOVA model and testing assumptions

TALL_ALIVE <- TALL6 |> filter(tht != 0.0) #creating dataframe with only alive saplings w/ recorded height data 

TALL_ALIVE |> ggplot() + aes(x = ttreatment, y = tht) +
  geom_boxplot()
##graphing: 

hist(TALL_ALIVE$tht) #histogram of height, skewed a bit right even w/ outliers removed

TALL_ALIVE |> ggplot() + aes(x = ttreatment, y = tht) + 
  geom_boxplot() #looking at my alive sapling heights, AC and NR don't seem to be super normal 

TALL_ALIVE |> group_by(ttreatment) |> count() #checking sample sizes to make sure NR group isn't being weird, pretty similar... 


##making linear model: 

height_m <- lm(tht ~ ttreatment + tblock, data = TALL_ALIVE) #creating linear model

plot(height_m)  #residuals are looking pretty good lwk, qq could be better :/ 

summary(height_m) #NR treatment most significant! 

##homogeniety test: 

shapiro.test(height_m$residuals) #checking the shapiro test to get a feel, only have 66 observations so it shouldn't be super crazy,,, 
#shapiro test p = 0.3388

#tried to do levenes test but it didn't like when my formula had a + interaction? it would only accept an interaction with * for some reason 
```

```{r, ANOVA test}

aov_heightm <- aov(tht ~ ttreatment + tblock, TALL_ALIVE) #running ANOVA

summary(aov_heightm)  #lookin at results 

TukeyHSD(aov_heightm) #lookin at the results but better

#takeaways: 
    #significant differences: 
      #NR-AC, p = 0.0000000
      #NR-DT, p = 0.0000000
      #OS-NR, p = 0.0000002
    #super similar: 
      #OS-DT, p = 0.9928696
    #overall natural recruits are doing some crazy stuff and no other treatment comes close to them,,, wacky


#####redoing linear model with NO NATURAL RECRUITS: 

TALL_NONR <- TALL6 |> filter(ttreatment != "NR") #removing natural recruits 

aov_heightnonrm <- aov(tht ~ ttreatment + tblock, TALL_NONR) #running ANOVA

summary(aov_heightnonrm)  #lookin at results 

TukeyHSD(aov_heightnonrm)

#takeaways: 
      #nothing is significant!!!!!!! 
      #most similar: DT-AC, p = 0.8742861
      #most different: OS-AC, p = 0.2602094
```

```{r, rough ANOVA plot}

#setting up summary table: 
height_m_summary <- TALL_ALIVE |> 
  group_by(ttreatment) |> 
  summarize( 
    mean = mean(tht), 
    se = sd(tht) / sqrt (length(tht)))  #height mean and standard error

height_m_summary #lookin


#####plotting violin w/ results: 

violin_anova <- TALL_ALIVE |> ggplot() + 
  aes(x = ttreatment, y = tht, fill = ttreatment ) + 
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5) + 
  stat_summary(fun = "mean", 
               geom = "point") + #marking avgs in each group
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", 
               geom = "errorbar", aes(width = 0.2)) + #error bars
  theme(legend.position = "none")

violin_anova

#adding labels and significance + stuff: 

violin_anova + labs(
  title = "ANVOA Results: Seedling Heights by Microhabitat", 
  x = "Microhabitat type", 
  y = "Seedling Height (cm)") +  #nice titles 
  scale_x_discrete( #renaming microhabitat types 
    labels = c("Adult Canopy", "Woody Debris", "Natural Recruit", "Open Space")
  ) + 
  #adding significance CLD labels: 
  annotate("text", 
           x = "AC", y = 26, label = "A") + 
  annotate("text", 
           x = "DT", y = 26, label = "A") + 
  annotate("text", 
           x = "NR", y = 37, label = "B") + 
  annotate("text", 
           x = "OS", y = 26, label = "A") 

ggsave(filename = "height_anova_violin.png",  plot = get_last_plot(), width = 6, height = 4)  #savin it 
```

## Regression Analysis:

```{r}

#looking at moisture data 
MOIST5 |> ggplot() + aes(x = mtreatment, y = vwc_mean) + 
  geom_boxplot() + facet_wrap(~mdate)


```

### splitting data wet/dry:

```{r}

#dropping NR from moisture data: 
MOIST_N0 <- MOIST5 |> filter(mtreatment != "NR")

##splitting height data by wet/dry 

WET_TALL <- TALL_NONR |> filter(tdate == "2026-10-15") |> 
  select(tdate, block_treat_mean) #taking just the date and the mean because I can

DRY_TALL <- TALL_NONR |> filter(tdate != "2026-10-15") |> 
  select(tdate, block_treat_mean) 

#splitting moisture data by wet/dry: 

WET_MOIST <- MOIST_N0 |> filter(mdate == "2026-10-21")

DRY_MOIST <- MOIST_N0 |> filter(mdate != "2026-10-21") #the dates on the soil moisture data are different,,,, girl

```

### wet regression:

```{r}
#DROP NR TREATMENT FROM SOIL MOISTURE REGRESSION AND STUFF 

#joining wet data: 
WET_JOIN <- full_join(WET_MOIST, WET_TALL,
                      by = c('mblock' = 'tblock', 
                             'mtreatment' = 'ttreatment')) |> select(
                               mdate, mblock, mtreatment, vwc_mean, block_treat_mean
                             ) |> drop_na(mdate)


#setting up linear model: 
WET_MODEL <- lm(block_treat_mean ~ vwc_mean, data = WET_JOIN)

summary(WET_MODEL)

plot(WET_MODEL) 

#getting coefficents for plot: 
summary(WET_MODEL)$r.squared    # 0.1113459
summary(WET_MODEL)$coefficients #slope = 0.3383019, intercept = 10.4355425  

#looking at anova: 
WET_ANOVA <- aov(vwc_mean ~ mtreatment+ mblock, data = WET_JOIN)

summary(WET_ANOVA)

TukeyHSD(WET_ANOVA) #tukey test on WET anova 
#takeaways: 
  #OS-AC, p = 0.0000000
  #DT-AC, p = 0.0001724
  #OS-DT, p = 0.0643769
```

```{r}
######regression point plot
wet_plot <- WET_JOIN |> ggplot() + aes(x = vwc_mean, y = block_treat_mean) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(title = "Wet Observations: Mean VWC vs. Mean Seedling Height",  #nice labels 
       x = "VWC %", 
       y = "Seedling Height (cm)") + 
  geom_text(x = 10, y = 1, label = "R-squared = 0.11, y = 0.34x + 10.44") #adding equation from model coefficients 

wet_plot

ggsave(filename = "wet_reg_plot.png",  plot = wet_plot, width = 6, height = 4)
```

### dry regression:

```{r}

#joining dry data: 
DRY_JOIN <- full_join(DRY_MOIST, DRY_TALL,
                      by = c('mblock' = 'tblock', 
                             'mtreatment' = 'ttreatment')) |> select(
                               mdate, mblock, mtreatment, vwc_mean, block_treat_mean
                             ) |> filter(mtreatment != "NR") |> drop_na(mdate)
#^^^^ joining datasets, selecting columns i want, DROPPING NR treatment, dropping NAs 

#setting up linear model: 
DRY_MODEL <- lm(block_treat_mean ~ vwc_mean, data = DRY_JOIN)

summary(DRY_MODEL)

plot(DRY_MODEL)

#getting coefficents for plot: 
summary(DRY_MODEL)$r.squared    #  0.09554909
summary(DRY_MODEL)$coefficients #slope = 1.196139, intercept = 6.134646  

#looking at anova: 
DRY_ANOVA <- aov(vwc_mean ~ mtreatment+ mblock, data = DRY_JOIN)

summary(DRY_ANOVA)

TukeyHSD(DRY_ANOVA)#tukey on dry observations
#most different: 
  #DT-AC: 0.0000497
  #DT-AC: 0.0031218
#most similar: 
  #OS-AC: 0.5229060

```

```{r}
#PLOTTING: 
dry_plot <- DRY_JOIN |> ggplot() + aes(x = vwc_mean, y = block_treat_mean) +
  geom_point() + geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) + 
  labs(title = "DRY REGRESSION") + 
  theme(legend.position = "none") + 
  labs(title = "Dry Observations: Mean VWC vs. Mean Seedling Height",  #nice labels 
       x = "VWC %", 
       y = "Seedling Height (cm)") + 
  geom_text(x = 2.5, y = 5, label = "R-squared = 0.10, y = 1.20x + 6.13") #adding equation 

ggsave(filename = "dry_reg_plot.png", plot = dry_plot,  width = 6, height = 4)
```

```{r}
#trying to make nice tables for anovas and tukeys: 

summary(WET_ANOVA)

#sumamrizing each anova: 
wetaov_summ <- anova_summary(WET_ANOVA)
dryaov_summ <- anova_summary(DRY_ANOVA) 

#checking results: 
wetaov_summ
# Effect DFn DFd      F        p p<.05   ges
# 1 trt  2   2  62 23.738 2.21e-08     1 0.434
# 2      1   3  62 10.282 1.38e-05     1 0.332
dryaov_summ
# Effect DFn DFd     F     p p<.05   ges
# 1 trt  2   2  47 5.236 0.009     1 0.182
# 2      1   3  47 2.994 0.040     1 0.160


combineaov_summ <- bind_rows(wetaov_summ, dryaov_sum) #combinging anova summaries 

combineaov_summ <- combineaov_summ [ c(1,3), ]  #dropping rows with block values 

combineaov_summ  #checkin 

#making into a nice table! 
gt(combineaov_summ)

#putting tukey results in table: 

#dry: 
dry_tukey <- TukeyHSD(DRY_ANOVA)
drytukey_df <- dry_tukey$mtreatment |> as.data.frame() |> round(digits = 2)#convert to df 
drytukey_df<- drytukey_df |>  rownames_to_column(var = "treatments") |> 
  select(treatments, diff, "p adj")

drytukey_df


#wet: 
wet_tukey <- TukeyHSD(WET_ANOVA) 
wettukey_df <- wet_tukey$mtreatment |> as.data.frame() |> round(digits = 2)
wettukey_df<- wettukey_df |>  rownames_to_column(var = "treatments") |> 
  select(treatments, diff, "p adj") 

#combing wet and dry tukey dfs: 
combinetukeys <- bind_rows(drytukey_df, wettukey_df)

combinetukeys


#making the ultimate tukey table: 
gtcombine <- gt(combinetukeys) |> tab_header(title = "Soil Moisture Tukey's HSD Results") |> #titling table
  tab_row_group("Wet Observations", c(4:6)) |>  #seperating wet data
  tab_options(row_group.default_label = "Dry Observations") |> 
  #changing column names: 
  cols_label( treatments = "Microhabitat Type",
              diff = "Difference", 
              "p adj" = "p-Value")

gtcombine

#setting up significance stars ***: 
stars = c("ns", "ns", "**", "***", "***", "ns")

#replacing treatment acronyms: 
gtcombine <- gtcombine |> sub_values(columns = treatments,
                        values = "DT-AC", 
                        replacement = "Woody Debris - Adult Canopy")|>
              sub_values(columns = treatments,
                         values = "OS-AC", 
                         replacement = "Open Space - Adult Canopy") |> 
              sub_values(columns = treatments,
                         values = "OS-DT", 
                         replacement = "Open Space - Woody Debris") |> 
  #adding nice divider and meessing with spacing between values
  gt_add_divider(columns = treatments) |>   opt_horizontal_padding(scale = 3) |> 
  #adding significance star column: 
  cols_add( Significance = stars)
  



gtsave(gtcombine, filename = "tukey_table.png")


```
